key_insight: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method couples porous-solid deformation, fluid flow, electrostatics, and ionic transport while retaining poroelastic stability near incompressibility.
engineering_relevance: The formulation directly approximates stresses and transport fluxes needed to analyze charged, saturated, deformable porous materials.
method: Reformulate mechanics using non-symmetric pseudostress and displacement, with mixed Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations.
Discretize with conforming Raviart–Thomas elements and discontinuous polynomials; reconstruct displacement gradients and Cauchy stress algebraically.
Use a residual-based error estimator to guide adaptive refinement in two dimensions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical error bounds and numerical experiments on convergence, near-incompressibility robustness, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization, without quantitative results.
watch_item: Well-posedness and estimator reliability require stability and small-data assumptions; the coupled estimator analysis is limited to two dimensions.
paper_title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
